analysis:
The PR makes two small changes to .github/workflows/release-provider.yml. First, it adds a workflow-level env DARKBLOOM_PROVIDER_TOOLCHAIN: release (head lines 112-114), a non-secret selector that picks Xcode 27.2 for build, qualify and sign via scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh. Second, it changes the validation-lane assertion from build_sdk_version '27.0' to '27.2' (head ~1444). The supplied evidence is only base text for lines 1-1066 plus the patch excerpt, so the head-side lines near 112 and 1444 are not shown as numbered source.

I traced the surrounding signing chain in base lines 426-1000: signing toolchain selection, the build SDK equality check (BUILD_SDK_VERSION against PROVIDER_SDK_VERSION), the final-bytes VersionSDK check, the hardened-runtime entitlement checks, the get-task-allow absence check, and the keychain deletion before release code runs. None of it is weakened. The tightened SDK pin to 27.2 is consistent with the existing PROVIDER_SDK_VERSION comparison.

The new env var is job-global and visible to all steps, but it carries no secret and no untrusted input. The relevant threats are T-034 and T-013 (code identity and artifact integrity), TB-009, and A-017/A-011 (build qualification and binary hash registry). The change appears to constrain, not loosen, the build identity.

Unverified contracts for the next pass: whether prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh actually enforces Xcode 27.2 and sets PROVIDER_SDK_VERSION consistently with DARKBLOOM_PROVIDER_TOOLCHAIN=release; whether the qualification shard and build lanes (.github/actions/provider-release-build) honor the new env var; and whether any coordinator-side qualification expects SDK 27.0. These sit outside the supplied evidence, so I record them as open questions rather than findings.
